vars.problem_description: I am being garnished from Oregon Department of Unemployment for an overpayment of over $20,000 with a 1% interest added on each month. I had requested their hardship application and submitted the documents via email within the timeframe I was given. I was later called and told that I would be garnished under the pretense that when I submitted the documents, I did not follow the instructions for I needed to submit the documents And Call. She said that there was a note on her end that said I was to call by the women I spoke to who sent me the hardship application. I don’t remember the conversation that well but I don’t remember her saying I need to call. On the email she sent me, nothing says to call, I have read it over numerous times. If this was such an important step that determines garnishment or not, why wasn’t it stressed to the fullest? And only apparently verbally said. I felt like there was nothing I could do over the phone discussing this with the person I talked to. I don’t know how to navigate any of this. She even told me the amount that I would be paying each month and what they considered in their final decision and what was not considered in their final decision. Even telling me about the waiver for forgiveness of the overpayment that I submitted and how it was unlikely that it was going to get granted due to the category that it was put into. But all of that didn’t matter because I didn’t call. I’m 25 years old with other bills and living expenses, I’m not the best with finances and already have a lot of debt that I struggle to pay and I’m being asked to pay back money that I don’t have anymore that was given to me over the course of about 11 months during this pandemic with interest. I would like to request a lawyer who can help me with getting out of the garnishment.

vars.problem_description: I live in a Manufactured Home Park for ages 65 and over. There are issues with a creek and embankment erosion behind where 28 homes are located (including mine). Company owning the park has purchased more than 20 of the homes and indicated buyouts of Fair Market Value. The work on the creek side will requires homes to be removed/demolished. Work will be done in three Phases. Mine is newer home and in Phase 2. I wanted them to purchase it now so I could purchase a new home that the company owns and is located on the other side of community. They purchased a home in Phase 3 in April  so owner could move. After 2+ months of corresponding with them on an offer, they told me they wouldn't purchase mine as "It's not needed yet". Home cannot be sold to outside buyer because of the creek erosion issues already being permitted through Hamilton County to begin next year. What is my recourse? Would need info from lawyer familiar with Manufactured Home Laws, Seniors, etc.

I want to request a hearing and need advice as to whether I should have an attorney represent me, and if there is any point to pursuing a hearing based on the case information.

When I showed that this was not possible, since my uncle died two years prior, the investigator said in a recorded phone call that she did not need my response or to discuss it because it “was just a misunderstanding.” When I received the legal documents outlining the allegations and sanctions, the allegation had changed to I made her feel uncomfortable and confused by going on and on about my uncle. It is clear that once I could prove the allegation was untrue, the client’s story changed. The Board should have noted from there that she is an unreliable reporter. However, there were several other allegations that the Board took as true. The type that I cannot provide proof I did not do or say. But again, the way the investigator presented the allegations, I could not answer because I could not recall such generalities. When given the legal documents with details, I can say that I did not, and would not have done such things. I want to request a hearing and need advice as to whether I should have an attorney represent me, and if there is any point to pursuing a hearing based on the case information.

vars.problem_description: I need a lawyer who practices law in social security disability cases. I have been receiving benefits from social security disability insurance since 2013 and recently received a decision to stop my benefits. Social security reached their decision because they claimed my income was too high. I was working with a subsidy from my current employer that SSDI did not take into account according to their documents. I perceive that I still deserve to receive benefits and they have discontinued them. Furthermore they claimed that I became disqualified from benefits in 2018 so they are asking me to pay back an over-payment of $40,000. I have submitted a reconsideration request for their decision already. I have other assets in an investment account that I am scared they will take away from me for repayment. I only make about $2300 per month and do not have the money to pay SSDI back. It could be proven that my disability actually started in 2004, and I only started receiving benefits in 2013 without receiving any backpay. I suppose I may be able to recapture the years I did not collect benefits given that I was disabled then as well, however this is secondary but may be of value.

prompt.raw: I have personal loan debt between 18-20,000 dollars and am unable to pay my monthly payments for each loan. All of my money goes to rent and bills rather than my loans and I do not have enough afterwards to pay anything off. I have no liquifiable assets (I do not own property, stock shares, and only have one car which is in the process of repossession) and frankly am not sure if I can do anything BUT file for bankruptcy at this point. I am not sure what type would be the best for me in the situation and would like to talk to someone about it.
prompt.label: {{problem_description}}

response.output:
Classification:
  - Bankruptcy > Personal (2.50)
  - Debtor/Creditor > Debt Counseling/Workouts (1.70)

Follow-up Questions:
Q1: What do you most want to happen with your debts right now?
  • Wipe out (erase) my personal loans and get a fresh start
  • Try to keep my car and catch up over time with a payment plan
  • I’m not sure yet
Q2: What’s going on with your car and the repossession (when the lender takes the car)?
  • They already took the car
  • I still have the car, but they are trying to take it
  • I still have the car and repossession is not happening right now
  • Not sure
Q3: Besides the personal loans, do you have any other debts or other income coming in?
  • Credit cards
  • Medical bills
  • Student loans
  • Back taxes (taxes you still owe)
  • Child support or alimony
  • A car loan (money owed for a car)
  • A home loan or mortgage (money owed for a house)
  • Extra income (like a side job, benefits, or help from family/friends)
  • No, none of these
